definitions.definition: n=λ.toNat+1, where λ.toNat=max(λ,0) viewed as a natural number; when λ≥0 this is λ+1.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For each natural r, X_r=(1/(r! in C)) x^r; composition is the endomorphism product, the zeroth power is the identity.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For each natural r, Y_r=(1/(r! in C)) y^r.

definitions.type: integer-valued family indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For natural j, c_j is the integer cast of Nat.choose(λ.toNat,j). For λ≥0 this is binom(λ,j).

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V indexed by natural i,j≤λ.toNat
definitions.definition: A_ij=X_(λ.toNat−i) Y_(λ.toNat) X_(λ.toNat) Y_(λ.toNat−j), with the rightmost factor acting first.
U=V(K)=M⊗_Z K, the balanced tensor product of integer modules. Its K-action is a·(m⊗b)=m⊗(ab).

definitions.type: induced K-linear operator for a specified lattice-preserving complex-linear operator T
definitions.definition: For any complex-linear T:V→V with T(M)⊆M, T^K:U→U denotes the operator m⊗a↦T(m)⊗a, extended by the balanced tensor relations. This notation asserts no preservation of M by an arbitrary T; preservation must be established in the packet. It applies to x,y,h,X_r,Y_r,A_ij only where their preservation has been supplied or proved.

binders.type: complex-linear endomorphism of V satisfying T(M)⊆M

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the complex universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(C)
definitions.definition: U_Z is the unital integer subalgebra generated by the elements X_r and Y_r for all natural r, acting on V by the specified representation.

L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K, equipped, whenever the commutator relations and lattice stability in the original assumptions hold, with their induced commutator bracket and action on U. The bracket normalization is [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h, including characteristic 2.

inputs.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

Let A_ij^K denote the operator induced by A_ij|_M on U=M⊗_Z K and define F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1) A_ij^K for 0≤i,j≤λ. Then F_ij F_kl=δ_(jk)F_il and Σ_(i=0)^λ F_ii=Id_U. For 0≤r≤λ the induced divided powers satisfy (r! in K)X_r^K=(x^K)^r and (r! in K)Y_r^K=(y^K)^r.

binders.type: K-linear operator family defined by F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1) A_ij^K, where the A_ij^K are the induced operators specified in this statement

Every K-linear subspace W⊂U=M⊗_Z K invariant under the induced x,y,h operators is invariant under every F_ij=(binom(λ,j) in K)^(-1)(X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j))^K for 0≤i,j≤λ.

binders.type: family F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1) A_ij^K as specified by the complete displayed expression

inputs.statement: Let K be any field, U a finite-dimensional K-vector space and n∈N with dim_K U=n. Suppose F_ij∈End_K(U), indexed by i,j∈Fin n, satisfy F_ij F_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0) and Σ_i F_ii=Id. Every K-subspace W invariant under all F_ij is zero or U. No positivity hypothesis on n is needed for this dichotomy.

hypotheses: K is a field and U is a finite-dimensional K-vector space.
n is a natural number and dim_K U=n.
F_ij are K-linear endomorphisms indexed by Fin n with F_ij F_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0).
The diagonal sum Σ_i F_ii equals Id_U.
W is a K-linear subspace invariant under every F_ij.

inputs.statement: For every natural number r, X_r(M)⊆M and Y_r(M)⊆M. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M. The given endomorphism h=xy−yx also satisfies h(M)⊆M: for every m∈M, h(m)=x(y(m))−y(x(m)) belongs to M. Thus x,y,h and all X_r,Y_r restrict to Z-linear endomorphisms of M.

binders.type: element of the additive subgroup M

output.statement: The vector space V(K)=M⊗_Z K is nonzero, and every K-linear subspace invariant under the induced x,y,h is either zero or all of V(K), for all the original parameters including λ=0, p=2, and arbitrary fields K of characteristic p.

locals.type: family of K-linear endomorphisms of U indexed by Fin n×Fin n
locals.declaration: Reindex the N004 family F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1)A_ij^K along Fin n≃{0,…,λ}.
Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W⊂U.

argument.text: H001 and D001 give n=λ+1≥1, so the integers 0,…,λ correspond bijectively to Fin n. Reindex the N004 family by this bijection, obtaining F. N004 gives F_ijF_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0) and Σ_i F_ii=Id_U; equality of indices and finite sums are preserved by this bijection. N005 gives dim_K U=λ+1=n and U≠0, and hence finite dimensionality. N007 gives integer restrictions of x,y,h, so the induced actions mentioned in the conclusion are defined and are exactly D009's operators on U.

produces.statement: U is a nonzero finite-dimensional K-space with dim_K U=n. The K-linear family F indexed by Fin n satisfies F_ijF_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0) for all i,j,k,l∈Fin n and Σ_(i∈Fin n)F_ii=Id_U. The induced x,y,h are defined on U.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary K-subspace W and introduce L1: W is invariant under the induced x,y,h. Apply N006 to W. Its operators are the same F as here because N006 and N004 give the identical expression (c_j in K)^(-1)(X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j))^K; reindexing does not change the maps. Therefore W is invariant under every F_ij. Apply E001 with its field=K, space=U, natural parameter=n, operator family=F and subspace=W. H001 gives the field, F001 gives finite dimension n and both matrix-unit identities, and the preceding application of N006 gives invariance. E001 yields W=0 or W=U.

Discharge L1 and universally quantify W: every K-subspace invariant under the induced x,y,h is zero or U. Combine with the nonzero assertion in F001 and U=M⊗_Z K=V(K). H001 allowed every field of characteristic p and every 0≤λ<p. No step requires algebraic closure or distinct weights in K. When λ=0 the index set has one element; when p=2 the permitted λ are 0,1 and the same argument applies. This is exactly P, with the original induced action.

applications.bindings: Source field=K, source space=U=M⊗_Z K, source n=λ.toNat+1, source F=the N004 family reindexed by Fin n, and source W=the arbitrary subspace W in this step.
hypothesis_checks: H001 makes K a field; F001 gives finite dimensionality of U.
D001 makes n natural; F001 gives dim_K U=n.
N004 and the explicit reindexing in S001 give K-linear maps with F_ijF_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0).
N004 gives the diagonal identity, preserved by the reindexing in S001 and recorded in F001.
W is a K-linear subspace by its arbitrary introduction; under L1, N006 applied in S002 gives invariance under precisely this family.
